newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on currency woes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on currency woes.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen falling on Tuesday as weakness in regional currencies took the baht near record lows early on Tuesday morning, traders said.
Hit with baht weakness and domestic political concerns the SET Index fell 18.91 points, or 3.03 percent, on Monday to 604.34. The SET 50 ended at 45.36.
"I think for the most part this is macro-dominated with problems in the region affecting Thailand but there is nothing on the micro that is too reassuring," said a trader at a large regional house.
The baht slid to a lowest traded level of 32.60 per dollar early onshore from 32.40 late on Monday and fears surrounding the stability of the finance sector were again affecting sentiment, they said.
"It's a cocktail of more bad financial news seeping out of the market coupled with weakness in the region, and weakness in the U.S." the broker said.
